title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Priorat and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show DOQ Priorat or DOCa Priorat. Since 2009, Priorat has a place-based classification: Vi de Vila, village wine, from one of 12 villages, like Gratallops or Porrera; Vinya Classificada, classified vineyard; and Gran Vinya Classificada, the top level. It was among the first in Spain to classify by place.
steps.highlight: Vi de Vila to Gran Vinya Classificada

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Priorat's power suits rich, savoury food: grilled lamb, wild boar, beef stews, Catalan dishes like duck with pears, and aged cheese. Serve at 16 to 18 degrees, decanted. Good Priorat ages 10 to 20 years, softening its alcohol and tannin into dried fruit and earth.

steps.prompt: What is Vi de Vila in Priorat?
options: A village wine from one of 12 villages

steps.body: Decant young Priorat for an hour or two. Its high alcohol and concentration open up with air.

steps.prompt: Which are levels of Priorat's classification?
steps.explanation: Gran Reserva Especial isn't a Priorat term.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Priorat classifies villages and vineyards since 2009
Its power suits lamb, boar and stews
Decant young Priorat; it ages 10 to 20 years
